description: We are a team of four participants from **Çankaya Science and Art Center (BİLSEM), Türkiye**. We are passionate about biology, biotechnology, scientific research, and exploring how science can help us better understand and improve the world around us.
summary:
We have developed a wearable health monitoring system designed to support astronauts' physical and psychological well-being during space
missions. The system uses an arm-mounted skin sensor, individually calibrated according to each astronaut's personal baseline values. Rather
than relying on general health standards, it continuously evaluates astronauts' health based on their individual data. It detects potential problems
and provides step-by-step guidance on how to respond. Based on health data, the system also aims to support water and electrolyte delivery
through wearable technology. Medication and injections, however, require medical approval. An integrated AI-powered chatbot provides
psychological support, helping astronauts cope with emotional challenges. Our project addresses critical space-related health risks, including
muscle and bone loss, changes in gait and balance, reduced thirst perception, electrolyte imbalances, fatigue, mood fluctuations, and limited
access to immediate medical assistance from Earth. By combining personalized monitoring, AI-powered guidance, and wearable technology, our
system aims to offer a proactive, practical, and comprehensive approach to astronaut health management.
details: ASTRA is developed for astronauts to monitor their health. It helps astronauts in various ways. Firstly, a device which is located on an astronaut's body rapidly measures the nutrient values in blood, oxygen level, blood sugar, pressure, etc. By analyzing the results it assigns a normal level for all values. If there are any anomalous results, it gives an alert to inform the astronaut. In order to solve the problem it gives in the required nutrients. Secondly, microgravity causes the bones and muscles of the astronauts to get weaker. With the same device the movements of the bones and muscles are being analyzed and if any negative differences are detected the monitor warns the astronaut to do specific exercises. Thirdly, to prevent astronauts from being depressed and becoming isolated there is an AI Bot to chat with the astronaut. Additionally, this AI will have psychological information to detect any psychological problems being possible to occur by analyzing the astronauts sound while talking so it will also talk to the astronaut with an intend of solving the problem. Furthermore, there is a body monitor which has color codes. If a part of the body is pretty healthy, that part is colored in green. However, if there is a problem with a part, that part is colored in red and when we click on that part we can see what the problem is and how to solve it. Lastly, with a part named ASTRA AI, we can easily reach the solution of a problemç For example, if your astronaut colleague suddenly faints, you can write what happened before and what were the symptoms to the AI so it will give out the problem and guide you to solve it. Our main goal is to provide a basic but practical monitor for astronauts to help them stay healthy while having a space mission. We were inspired by the Type-1 Diabetes devices and insulin pumps. We used Claud AI to create a prototype of our monitor.
